accepted.context_brief: cluster points for decreasing bounded approximants
accepted.question_text: Let phi be an arbitrary plurisubharmonic function on a domain Omega contained in C^n. When (phi_j) is any sequence of bounded plurisubharmonic functions that decreases to phi, determine what can be said about the set of cluster points of the Monge-Ampere measures (dd^c phi_j)^n.

evidence.quote: Question 1 (Bedford). Given phi an arbitrary plurisubharmonic function in some domain Omega subset C^n, what can be said about the set of cluster points of (dd^c phi_j)^n, where phi_j are bounded plurisubharmonic functions which decrease to phi ?

accepted.question_text: Let phi be a bounded plurisubharmonic function on a domain Omega contained in C^n. When (phi_j) is any sequence of bounded plurisubharmonic functions converging to phi in L^1_loc, determine what can be said about the set of cluster points of the Monge-Ampere measures (dd^c phi_j)^n.

evidence.quote: Question 2 (Bedford). Given phi a bounded plurisubharmonic function in some domain Omega subset C^n, what can be said about the set of cluster points of (dd^c phi_j)^n, where phi_j are bounded plurisubharmonic functions which converge to phi in L^1_loc ?

accepted.context_brief: locality of maximality for psh functions
accepted.question_text: Decide whether maximality is a local property for arbitrary plurisubharmonic functions; that is, whether maximality can always be checked locally rather than globally.

evidence.quote: Question 3 (Blocki). Is maximality a local notion for arbitrary plurisubharmonic functions?

accepted.context_brief: holomorphic foliation of maximal C2,alpha solutions
accepted.question_text: Assume 0 <= alpha < 1, n = 2, and phi is a maximal plurisubharmonic function of class C^{2,alpha}. Determine whether the support of dd^c phi is foliated or laminated by holomorphic discs along which phi is harmonic.

evidence.quote: Question 4 (Dujardin). Assume 0 <= alpha < 1 and n = 2. Assume phi is C^{2,alpha}-smooth and maximal. Is the support of dd^c phi foliated (or laminated) by holomorphic disc along which phi is harmonic ?

accepted.question_text: Characterize the global domain DMA(X, omega) of definition of the complex Monge-Ampere operator on a compact Kahler manifold (X, omega).

evidence.quote: Question 5 (Coman-Guedj-Zeriahi). Characterize DMA(X, omega).

accepted.context_brief: convexity and max stability of DMA
accepted.question_text: For a compact Kahler manifold (X, omega), determine whether DMA(X, omega) is convex and whether, whenever phi belongs to DMA(X, omega) and psi belongs to PSH(X, omega), the function max(phi, psi) must also belong to DMA(X, omega).

evidence.quote: Question 6 (Coman-Guedj-Zeriahi). Is DMA(X, omega) convex ? If phi in DMA(X, omega) and psi in PSH(X, omega), does it imply that max(phi, psi) in DMA(X, omega) ?

accepted.question_text: Let phi be a plurisubharmonic function on the unit ball B in C^n with well-defined complex Monge-Ampere measure. If (dd^c phi)^n has a Dirac mass at the origin, determine whether phi must have positive Lelong number at 0.

evidence.quote: Question 7 (Guedj, Rashkovskii). Assume that (dd^c phi)^n has a Dirac mass at the origin. Does it imply that phi has a positive Lelong number at 0 in C^n ?

accepted.question_text: Given a plurisubharmonic function phi on the unit ball and Demailly's Bergman-type approximants phi_j built from the weighted Bergman spaces H(j phi), determine whether the Monge-Ampere masses at the origin satisfy (dd^c phi_j)^n(0) -> (dd^c phi)^n(0).

evidence.quote: Question 8 (Demailly). Does one have (dd^c phi_j)^n (0) -> (dd^c phi)^n (0) ?

accepted.question_text: Let (X, omega) be complex projective space CP^n with the Fubini-Study Kahler form. Determine whether there exists an omega-plurisubharmonic function G_a in DMA(X, omega) whose Monge-Ampere measure is concentrated at a point a in CP^n and whose Lelong number at a is irrational.

evidence.quote: Question 9 (Coman-Guedj). Assume (X, omega) is the complex projective space CP^n equipped with the Fubini-Study Kahler form. Can one find examples of a omega-psh function G_a in DMA(X, omega), whose Monge-Ampere measure is concentrated at some point a in CP^n and having an irrational Lelong number at a ?

accepted.question_text: Suppose T and S are cohomologous positive closed currents with T more singular than S. Determine whether their non-pluripolar self-products satisfy <T^n> <= <S^n>.

evidence.quote: Question 10 (Boucksom-Eyssidieux-Guedj-Zeriahi). Assume T ~ S with T more singular than S. Is it true that <T^n> <= <S^n> ?

accepted.question_text: Let phi belong to DMA(X, omega) on a compact Kahler manifold, and assume its Monge-Ampere measure MA(phi) does not charge the polar set where phi = -infinity. Determine whether this implies that phi belongs to the full-mass energy class E(X, omega).

evidence.quote: Question 11 (Coman-Guedj-Zeriahi). Assume phi in DMA(X, omega) is such that MA(phi) does not charge (phi = -infinity). Does it imply that phi belongs to E(X, omega) ?

accepted.question_text: Let pi: X -> CP^2 be the blow-up of the complex projective plane at one point, let omega be a Kahler form in c_1(X), let D be a smooth anticanonical divisor, and let mu_D = omega wedge [D] / V be the normalized Lebesgue measure along D. Determine whether there exists phi_D in DMA(X, omega) such that MA(phi_D) = mu_D.

evidence.quote: Question 12 (Phong). Let X -> CP^2 be the blow up of the complex projective plane at one point. This is a DelPezzo surface, hence its first Chern class is positive. Pick omega in c1(X) a Kahler form, D a smooth anticanonical divisor, and let mu_D = omega wedge [D]/V denote a normalized Lebesgue measure along D. Can one find phi_D in DMA(X, omega) such that MA(phi_D) = mu_D ?

accepted.context_brief: range on bounded local psh functions
accepted.question_text: Determine whether the range of the complex Monge-Ampere operator acting on locally bounded plurisubharmonic functions is characterized by a uniform integrability condition.

evidence.quote: Question 13 (Bedford). Is the range of the complex Monge-Ampere operator acting on PSH intersect L^infty_loc characterized by a uniform integrability condition ?

accepted.context_brief: continuous subsolution implies continuous solution locally
accepted.question_text: Let mu be a probability measure on a bounded domain Omega in C^n. Assume there exists a continuous plurisubharmonic subsolution u on Omega with u|_{partial Omega} = 0 and mu <= (dd^c u)^n in Omega. Determine whether there must exist a continuous plurisubharmonic function phi on Omega with phi|_{partial Omega} = 0 and mu = (dd^c phi)^n in Omega.

evidence.quote: Question 14 (Kolodziej). Assume there is a continuous subsolution to the Dirichlet problem, i.e. there is a continuous psh function u in Omega such that u|_{partial Omega} = 0 and mu <= (dd^c u)^n in Omega. Does it imply that there is a continuous solution, i.e. a continuous psh function phi such that phi|_{partial Omega} = 0 and mu = (dd^c phi)^n in Omega ?

accepted.question_text: Let (X, omega) be a compact Kahler manifold, and let mu be a probability measure that is locally dominated by Monge-Ampere measures of bounded plurisubharmonic functions. Determine whether there exists phi in PSH(X, omega) intersect L^infty(X) such that mu = MA(phi).

evidence.quote: Question 15 (Kolodziej). Let (X, omega) be a compact Kahler manifold. Let mu be a probability measure which is locally dominated by the Monge-Ampere measures of bounded plurisubharmonic functions. Can one find phi in PSH(X, omega) intersect L^infty(X) such that mu = MA(phi) ?

accepted.question_text: For a compact Kahler manifold (X, omega) and a probability measure mu, determine whether the following are equivalent: first, there exists epsilon_mu > 0 such that exp(-epsilon_mu * PSH(X, omega)) is contained in L^1(mu); second, there exists a Holder continuous omega-plurisubharmonic function phi on X such that mu = MA(phi).

evidence.quote: Question 16 (DDGHKZ). Are the following properties equivalent ? (i) There exists epsilon_mu > 0 such that exp(-epsilon_mu PSH(X, omega)) subset L^1(mu). (ii) There exists phi in Hol(X, omega) such that mu = MA(phi).

accepted.context_brief: Holder subsolution implies Holder solution locally
accepted.question_text: Let mu be a probability measure on a bounded pseudoconvex domain Omega in C^n. Assume there exists a Holder continuous plurisubharmonic subsolution u on Omega with u|_{partial Omega} = 0 and mu <= (dd^c u)^n. Determine whether there must exist a Holder continuous plurisubharmonic function phi on Omega with phi|_{partial Omega} = 0 and mu = (dd^c phi)^n.

evidence.quote: Question 17 (Zeriahi). Let mu be a probability measure in a bounded pseudoconvex domain Omega subset C^n. Assume there is a Holder continuous subsolution to the Dirichlet problem, i.e. there is a Holder continuous psh function u in Omega such that u|_{partial Omega} = 0 and mu <= (dd^c u)^n in Omega. Is there a Holder continuous psh function phi such that phi|_{partial Omega} = 0 and mu = (dd^c phi)^n in Omega ?

accepted.context_brief: PDE proof of Kolodziej sup estimate
accepted.question_text: Give a proof, using PDE techniques, of the a priori estimate in Theorem 3.1: if B is the unit ball in C^n, p > 1, phi is a smooth plurisubharmonic function on B with phi|_{partial B} = 0, and det(phi_{j ar{k}}) = f, then ||phi||_{L^infty(B)} <= C ||f||_{L^p(B)}^{1/n}, where C depends only on n and p.

evidence.quote: Theorem 3.1. Let B be the unit ball of C^n and fix p > 1. If phi is a smooth plurisubharmonic function in B such that phi|_{partial B} = 0, then ||phi||_{L^infty(B)} <= C ||f||_{L^p(B)}^{1/n}, where det(phi_{jk}) = f and C only depends on n, p. Question 18 (Blocki-Kolodziej). Find a proof of the above estimate that relies on PDE techniques.

accepted.context_brief: Holder regularity for semipositive big classes
accepted.question_text: Let X be a compact Kahler manifold, let omega be a smooth semi-positive big (1,1)-form, and let phi solve (omega + dd^c phi)^n = f dV with f in L^p for some p > 1. Determine whether phi must be Holder continuous on all of X.

evidence.quote: Question 19 (Eyssidieux-Guedj-Zeriahi). Assume omega is merely semi-positive and big and (omega + dd^c phi)^n = f dV, f in L^p, p > 1. Is phi Holder continuous on X ?

accepted.question_text: Let (X, omega) be a compact n-dimensional Kahler manifold, let S be a smooth totally real submanifold of maximal real dimension n, let mu_S be its normalized Hausdorff measure, and let phi_S in E(X, omega) be the unique normalized omega-plurisubharmonic potential with (omega + dd^c phi_S)^n = mu_S. Determine the optimal regularity of phi_S.

evidence.quote: Let mu_S denote the normalized n-dimensional Hausdorff measure on a smooth totally real manifold S subset X of maximal real dimension n. It has been shown by Sadullaev in [Sad76] that S is non pluripolar, hence mu_S is the Monge-Ampere measure mu_S = (omega + dd^c phi_S)^n of a unique function phi_S in E(X, omega) normalized by sup_X phi_S = 0. Question 20 (Berman). What is the optimal regularity of phi_S ?

accepted.context_brief: smoothness on ample locus for big classes
accepted.question_text: Let alpha in H^{1,1}(X, R) be a big cohomology class on a compact manifold in the Fujiki class, let mu be a smooth volume form, and let T be the unique finite-energy current in alpha satisfying <T^n> = mu. Determine whether T is smooth on the ample locus Amp(alpha).

evidence.quote: Question 21. Let alpha in H^{1,1}(X, R) be a big cohomology class, mu a smooth volume form and let T be the unique finite energy current in alpha such that <T>^n = mu. Is T smooth in Amp(alpha) ?

accepted.question_text: Let (X, omega) be a compact n-dimensional Kahler manifold, and let phi in E(X, omega) solve (omega + dd^c phi)^n = f omega^n where f is L^1 and smooth away from a divisor D subset X. Determine whether phi is smooth on X minus D.

evidence.quote: Question 22 (DiNezza-Lu). Let (X, omega) be a compact n-dimensional Kahler manifold. Assume phi in E(X, omega) solves the equation (omega + dd^c phi)^n = f omega^n, with f in L^1 being smooth off a divisor D subset X. Is the function phi smooth on X \ D?

accepted.question_text: Let Omega be a bounded hyperconvex domain in C^n, and let u be the unique continuous plurisubharmonic function on Omega with boundary value 0 and Monge-Ampere equation (dd^c u)^n = f dV, where f is smooth and bounded below by a positive constant. Determine whether u is automatically smooth.

evidence.quote: Question 23 (Blocki). Let Omega subset C^n be a bounded hyperconvex domain. Let u be the unique continuous plurisubharmonic function in Omega such that u|_{partial Omega} = 0 and (dd^c u)^n = f dV, with f smooth and bounded away from zero f >= epsilon > 0. Is u automatically smooth ?

accepted.question_text: Let Omega be a smooth strictly pseudoconvex bounded domain in C^n, and let u be a plurisubharmonic solution of class C^{1,alpha}(Omega) with alpha > 1 - 2/n satisfying (dd^c u)^n = f dV, where f is smooth and bounded below by a positive constant. Determine whether u must in fact be smooth.

evidence.quote: Question 24 (Blocki-Dinew). Let u be a plurisubharmonic function in a smooth strictly pseudoconvex bounded domain Omega subset C^n. Assume u in C^{1,alpha}(Omega), alpha > 1 - 2/n and (dd^c u)^n = f dV, with f smooth and bounded away from zero f >= epsilon > 0. Is u automatically smooth ?

accepted.question_text: Let Omega be a smooth strictly pseudoconvex bounded domain in C^n, let varphi belong to C^{1,1}(partial Omega), and let u be the unique plurisubharmonic function on Omega, continuous up to the boundary, with u = varphi on partial Omega and (dd^c u)^n = 0 in Omega. Prove by complex-analytic methods that u is C^{1,1} on Omega.

evidence.quote: Question 25 (Demailly). Fix Omega subset C^n a smooth strictly pseudoconvex bounded domain, and phi in C^{1,1}(partial Omega). Let u be the unique plurisubharmonic function in Omega, continuous up to the boundary, such that u = phi on partial Omega and (dd^c u)^n = 0 in Omega. Show, by using complex analytic methods, that u is C^{1,1}-smooth in Omega.

accepted.question_text: In the setting of Theorem 3.5, let Omega be a C^{3,1} smooth strictly pseudoconvex bounded domain in C^n, let phi belong to C^{3,1}(partial Omega), and let u be the unique plurisubharmonic function on Omega, continuous up to the boundary, solving (dd^c u)^n = f in Omega with f >= 0 and f^{1/n} in C^{1,1}(closure Omega). Determine the minimal assumptions under which u belongs to C^2(closure Omega).

evidence.quote: Theorem 3.5 (Krylov). Assume that Omega subset C^n is a C^{3,1} smooth strictly pseudoconvex bounded domain, and phi in C^{3,1}(partial Omega). Let u be the unique plurisubharmonic function in Omega, continuous up to the boundary, such that u = phi on partial Omega and (dd^c u)^n = f in Omega with f >= 0, f^{1/n} in C^{1,1}(closure Omega). Then u in C^{1,1}(closure Omega). ... Question 26. Under what minimal assumptions does u belong to C^2(closure Omega) ?

accepted.question_text: Let Omega be a bounded hyperconvex domain and let g_Omega(z,w) be its pluricomplex Green function with pole at w. Determine whether g_Omega(z,w) converges locally uniformly to 0 as the pole w approaches the boundary of Omega.

evidence.quote: Question 27 (Blocki). Is it true that for a bounded hyperconvex domain g_Omega(z, w) converges locally uniformly to zero, as the pole w converges to the boundary of Omega?

accepted.context_brief: non-C2 example for one-pole Green function
accepted.question_text: Let Omega be a smoothly bounded strictly pseudoconvex domain, and let g_Omega(.,w) be the pluricomplex Green function with one pole w. Since g_Omega is known to lie in C^{1,1}(Omega \ {w}), determine whether there exists an example for which g_Omega fails to be C^2 on Omega minus the pole.

evidence.quote: Question 28 (Blocki). Let Omega be smoothly bounded strictly pseudoconvex domain. It is known that g_Omega in C^{1,1}(Omega \ {w}). Is there an example where g fails to be in C^2(Omega \ {w})?

accepted.question_text: Let (X, omega) be a compact Hermitian manifold of complex dimension at least 3. Characterize the Hermitian forms omega for which the total volume integral_X (omega + dd^c phi)^n equals integral_X omega^n for every bounded omega-plurisubharmonic function phi.

evidence.quote: Question 29 (Dinew-Kolodziej). Let (X, omega) be a compact Hermitian manifold of dimension greater or equal to 3. Characterize the forms omega for which integral_X (omega + dd^c phi)^n = integral_X omega^n for any bounded omega-plurisubharmonic function phi.

accepted.question_text: For a compact Hermitian manifold (X, omega), define T(X, omega) as the infimum of integral_X (omega + dd^c phi)^n over smooth omega-plurisubharmonic functions phi. Determine whether T(X, omega) can be equal to 0 for some manifold.

evidence.quote: Question 30 (Tosatti). Let (X, omega) be a compact Hermitian manifold. Define T(X, omega) by T(X, omega) = inf { integral_X (omega + dd^c phi)^n | phi in C^infty(X) intersect PSH(X, omega) }. Is it possible that T(X, omega) = 0 for some manifold?

accepted.question_text: For a compact Hermitian manifold (X, omega), define cap(X, omega) as the infimum of integral_X (omega + dd^c phi)^n over omega-plurisubharmonic functions phi with 0 <= phi <= 1. Relate this quantity to the geometry of (X, omega), determine whether it can be computed from geometric data, and determine how it behaves under deformations.

evidence.quote: Question 31 (Dinew-Kolodziej). Let (X, omega) be a compact Hermitian manifold. Define cap(X, omega) by cap(X, omega) = inf { integral_X (omega + dd^c phi)^n | phi in PSH(X, omega), 0 <= phi <= 1 }. Relate the quantity cap(X, omega) to the geometry of (X, omega). In particular is this quantity computable in terms of geometric data? How does it behave under deformations?

accepted.context_brief: remove lower bound in Hermitian stability theorem
accepted.question_text: In Theorem 4.3 for Hermitian Monge-Ampere equations, u and v are continuous omega-plurisubharmonic solutions with right-hand sides f and g in L^p, and the stability estimate ||u - v||_infty <= C ||f - g||_p^alpha is proved under the extra assumption f >= c_0 > 0. Determine whether that lower-bound assumption on f can be removed.

evidence.quote: Theorem 4.3 (Kolodziej-Nguyen). ... Assume moreover that f >= c0 for some c0 > 0. Then ||u - v||_infty <= C ||f - g||_p^alpha ... Question 32 (Kolodziej-Nguyen). Can one remove the condition f >= c0 > 0 ?

accepted.context_brief: prescribed logarithmic poles on Hermitian manifolds
accepted.question_text: Let z_1, ..., z_k be points on a Hermitian manifold X, and let tau_1, ..., tau_k be positive numbers satisfying sum_j tau_j^n < integral_X omega^n. Construct an omega-plurisubharmonic function phi such that near each z_j one has phi(z) <= tau_j log ||z - z_j|| + O(1).

evidence.quote: Question 33 (Tosatti-Weinkove). Let z1, ..., zk be a collection of points on a Hermitian manifold X and let tau1, ..., tauk be a collection of positive numbers satisfying sum_j tau_j^n < integral_X omega^n. Construct an omega-plurisubharmonic function, so that phi(z) <= tau_j log(||z - z_j||) + O(1) near z_j.

accepted.question_text: Determine whether quasi-plurisubharmonic functions can be desingularized in every complex dimension n >= 3 in the same sense known in dimensions at most 2, namely after suitable blow-ups separating divisorial singularities from a residual positive current with arbitrarily small Lelong numbers.

evidence.quote: Question 34 (Favre-Guedj-Jonsson). Can one similarly desingularize quasi-plurisubharmonic functions in any dimension n >= 3 ?

accepted.question_text: Let Omega be a bounded hyperconvex domain and phi belong to the Cegrell class F(Omega). If lambda^n = integral_Omega (dd^c phi)^n, determine whether the sublevel volumes satisfy the sharper estimate Vol({phi < -s}) <= c_n * delta_Omega^{2n} * exp(-2 n s lambda^{-1}) for all s > 0, without the polynomial prefactor appearing in the known theorem.

evidence.quote: Theorem 5.1 (Ahag, Cegrell, Hiep, Kolodziej, Zeriahi). There is a uniform constant c_n, such that for any s > 0 and any phi in F(Omega) one has Vol({phi < -s}) <= c_n delta_Omega^{2n} (1 + s lambda^{-1})^{n-1} exp(-2 n s lambda^{-1}), with lambda^n = integral_Omega (dd^c phi)^n. Question 35 (ACHKZ). Is it true that (for a different constant c_n) Vol({phi < -s}) <= c_n delta_Omega^{2n} exp(-2 n s lambda^{-1}) ?

accepted.question_text: Let X be a compact Kahler manifold, or more generally a manifold in the Fujiki class, and let omega be a smooth semi-positive big (1,1)-form. If phi belongs to the finite-energy class E(X, omega), determine whether phi has zero Lelong number at every point.

evidence.quote: Question 36 (Berman-Boucksom-Eyssidieux-Guedj-Zeriahi). Assume phi in E(X, omega) is a omega-psh function with finite energy. Is it true that phi has zero Lelong number at all points ?

accepted.question_text: Let (X, omega) be a compact Kahler manifold and Y a complex submanifold. Determine whether every omega|_Y-plurisubharmonic function on Y is the restriction to Y of some omega-plurisubharmonic function on X.

evidence.quote: Question 37 (Coman-Guedj-Zeriahi). Is it true that PSH(Y, omega|_Y) = PSH(X, omega)|_Y ?

accepted.context_brief: extend singular semipositive metrics in families
accepted.question_text: Consider a smooth holomorphic family pi: X -> Delta of compact Kahler manifolds and a pseudoeffective line bundle L -> X. If h_0 = e^{-phi_0} is a singular Hermitian metric on L_0 = L|_{X_0} with semi-positive curvature current dd^c phi_0 >= 0, determine whether there exists a Hermitian metric h = e^{-phi} on L over all of X such that dd^c phi >= 0 and phi restricts to phi_0 on X_0.

evidence.quote: Question 38 (Paun). Can one find h = e^{-phi} a hermitian metric of L on X which is a semi-positive extension of phi_0, i.e. such that dd^c phi >= 0 and phi|_{X_0} = phi_0 ?

accepted.question_text: For a plurisubharmonic function phi on a bounded pseudoconvex domain, determine what can be said about the set of points where phi admits no differential test from above; in particular, determine whether that set has zero Lebesgue measure or zero capacity.

evidence.quote: Question 39 (Guedj-Zeriahi). Let phi be a plurisubharmonic function. What can be said about the set of points at which phi does not admit a differential test from above ? It is known that this set has empty interior. Is it of zero Lebesgue measure (or capacity) ?

accepted.question_text: Let v be a continuous viscosity supersolution of the local complex Monge-Ampere equation -(dd^c V)^n + f dV = 0 on a bounded domain. If P(v) denotes the plurisubharmonic envelope of v, determine whether P(v) is a pluripotential supersolution of the same equation.

evidence.quote: Question 40 (Eyssidieux-Guedj-Zeriahi). Let v be a continuous viscosity supersolution of the equation -(dd^c V)^n + f dV = 0. Is P(v) a pluripotential supersolution of the same equation ?

accepted.context_brief: smooth approximation in semipositive big class
accepted.question_text: Let omega be a smooth semi-positive big (1,1)-form on a compact Kahler manifold X. Determine whether every function phi in PSH(X, omega) is the decreasing limit of smooth omega-plurisubharmonic functions.

evidence.quote: Question 41 (Eyssidieux-Guedj-Zeriahi). Let omega be a smooth semi-positive and big form on a compact Kahler manifold X. Is any function phi in PSH(X, omega) the decreasing limit of smooth omega-psh functions ?

accepted.question_text: Let alpha be a big cohomology class on a compact Kahler manifold, let theta be a smooth closed representative of alpha, and let V_theta be the theta-plurisubharmonic function with minimal singularities. Determine whether the polar locus P(alpha) = {x : V_theta(x) = -infinity} always coincides with the non-bounded locus NB(alpha) = {x : V_theta is not locally bounded near x}.

evidence.quote: Question 42 (Eyssidieux-Guedj-Zeriahi). Does P(alpha) always coincide with NB(alpha) ?

accepted.question_text: Let X be a compact Kahler manifold, let alpha_0 be a Kahler class, and let S_0 be a positive closed current representing alpha_0 with possibly nonzero Lelong numbers. Di Nezza and Lu construct a maximal weak Kahler-Ricci flow (omega_t)_{0 < t < T_max} that is smooth on time-increasing Zariski open sets. Determine whether this flow produces approximants with analytic singularities.

evidence.quote: When S0 has some non-zero Lelong numbers, DiNezza and Lu construct a maximal family of positive currents (omega_t)_{0<t<Tmax} which are honest Kahler forms on a time-increasing family of Zariski open subsets Omega_t where they satisfy the Kahler-Ricci flow equation. By analogy with Demailly regularization results, it is natural to expect that this family has analytic singularities. Question 43 (DiNezza-Lu). Does the Kahler-Ricci flow produce approximants with analytic singularities ?

accepted.context_brief: run local Monge-Ampere flow from arbitrary psh data
accepted.question_text: For the complex Monge-Ampere flow in a bounded smooth strictly pseudoconvex domain, Do proved existence and smoothing when the initial datum u_0 is bounded and plurisubharmonic on a neighborhood of the domain. Determine whether the flow can be started from an arbitrary plurisubharmonic initial function, not necessarily bounded.

evidence.quote: These flows can thus be run from a bounded plurisubharmonic initial data. The following question is natural, in view of the corresponding global results from [GZ13, DiNL14b]: Question 44 (Guedj). Can one run the above complex Monge-Ampere flow from an arbitrary plurisubharmonic function ?

accepted.context_brief: comparison principle for degenerate parabolic flow
accepted.question_text: Consider the degenerate complex Monge-Ampere flow (omega_t + dd^c phi_t)^n = exp(dot(phi_t) + F(t, x, phi)) mu(t, x) on [0, T] x X, where omega_t is a continuous family of semi-positive big (1,1)-forms bounded below by a fixed semi-positive big form, F is continuous and nondecreasing in the last variable, and mu is a bounded continuous volume form. If u is a bounded upper semicontinuous viscosity subsolution and v is a bounded lower semicontinuous viscosity supersolution with u <= v on the parabolic boundary {0} x X, determine whether u <= v holds on all of [0, T] x X.

evidence.quote: Question 45 (Eyssidieux-Guedj-Zeriahi). Assume u (resp. v) is a viscosity subsolution (resp. supersolution) to the above degenerate complex Monge-Ampere flow such that u <= v on the parabolic boundary {0} x X. Is it true that u <= v on [0, T] x X ?
